rules.sentence: If no shunt is present, only the right side of the heart will be pacified because the air bubbles will be too small to traverse the lungs.
Because PFO is a one-way flap, maneuvers should be used to temporarily increase right atrial pressure.
Either a Valsalva maneuver or sniff maneuver can be effective.

Color flow Doppler echocardiography is usually sufficient for diagnosis of a secundum-type atrial septal defect, but agitated saline is the generally needed for the diagnosis of other types of atrial septal defects.
In patients with either atrial or ventricular septal defects, estimation of the severity of the left-to-right shunt is essential and can be an important determinant in management decisions.
Ventricular septal defects can generally be visualized by color flow Doppler as turbulent high-velocity jets from the left to the right ventricle.
In cases where the jet origin is unclear, continuous wave Doppler can estimate the velocities.
These would be expected to be noted in the subcostal view with color flow Doppler showing flow through the defect (right).
Shunts are generally assessed by echocardiography by assessing the relationship between pulmonary flow and aortic flow, the Qp/Qs ratio.
